rated_messages.input_message: Notice what it feels like to see other people smoke and choose not to smoke. Notice what thoughts or emotions come up. Allow them to come and go. They will pass and so will this urge.
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.

When you notice yourself trapped in stressful thoughts or worry, say out loud, "I'm noticing that I'm having some worrisome thoughts." This helps unhook you from your thoughts so you don't stay caught in them.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
Stop and take 3 deep breaths. Then decide if you really want to smoke right now or not. Pausing for a few breaths can help lessen the habit.
